newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-TOP EUROPEANS STILL SHOWING ENGLISH CLUBS THE WAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TOP EUROPEANS STILL SHOWING ENGLISH CLUBS THE WAY.

text.p: The failure of Manchester United and Liverpool to reach their respective European cup finals this week makes a mockery of claims that the English premier league is the strongest in Europe.
Throughout the soccer season, assorted media pundits offer the view that the English league is the most exciting and colourful in Europe.

But the elimination of Manchester United and Liverpool from the semifinals of the European Cup and Cup Winners' Cup this week, plus the earlier exits of Arsenal, Aston Villa and Newcastle United from the UEFA Cup, offer a harsher reality.

The truth is that while the English game has undergone a revolution since the Heysel, Bradford and Hillsborough disasters of the 1980s, leading English teams are still coming off second best against top European opponents.

Luck may play a part but consistently failing to convert scoring chances, a lack of mental resolve and naive tactical thinking also contribute. Manchester United lost five of the 10 European ties they played this season and they were not all down to bad luck.

Nor can it be a coincidence that they failed to score a goal in four matches against the two teams who made it to the European Cup Final, Juventus and Borussia Dortmund. Manchester United lost all four games against those two opponents 1-0.

Both Manchester United manager Alex Ferguson and Liverpool manager Roy Evans had immediate, valid reasons why their teams lost to Borussia and Paris Saint Germain respectively on Wednesday and Thursday.

Ferguson admitted that his team failed to take their chances in both the away and home legs against the Germans, while Evans said his team's worst performance of the season when they lost 3-0 in Paris two weeks ago, proved an insurmountable obstacle.
The fact that Liverpool clawed back their pride in their 2-0 second leg win on Thursday was some consolation and left Evans relatively upbeat.
"From an English point of view, from where we were a few years ago, criticised by everybody, to be where we are now is a positive step.
"But people are now beginning to expect things from English clubs. We have taken some giant steps and both Liverpool and Manchester United have reached the semifinals this season."
Evans's comment is valid only if related to the performance of English clubs since the lifting of the ban imposed on them after the Heysel Stadium disaster in 1985.

In the immediate period before Heysel English clubs reached eight European Cup finals in nine years, winning seven of them. In the 13 years before Heysel they also won the UEFA Cup five times. Since their return in 1990, no English side has reached the European Cup or UEFA Cup finals, although Manchester United (1991) and Arsenal (1994) have won the Cup Winners' Cup, generally regarded as the weakest of the three competitions.

Ferguson, who won the Cup Winners' Cup with Aberdeen in 1983 and longs to emulate Sir Matt Busby's 1968 achievement of winning the European Cup for United, often refers to the problems the Heysel ban caused English soccer.

"It is still having an effect but admittedly with each passing year the effect of the ban is diminished. But the shadow of the ban still casts its pall. Generally speaking, English clubs don't seem to play with the same confidence they had before the ban."
Ferguson is expected to spend his summer looking for a top-class striker to snap up the kind of chances United created to no avail both at home and away against Dortmund.
There is also some speculation that talismanic French captain Eric Cantona may be allowed to leave Old Trafford as Ferguson shapes a new side to try and bring the European Cup back to Manchester.
Meanwhile holders Juventus and Borussia Dortmund, containing the nucleus of the German side that won last year's European championship will meet in the final in Munich on May 28.

Juventus will be making their second successive appearance in the final. It will be the sixth successive season that an Italian club has appeared and the eighth time in nine seasons that an Italian side has reached the final.
England were able to boast a record like that once.
